records.people: Wilfredo Rafael Cerrato Rodríguez (President of the Banco Central de Honduras from 27 January 2018)
records.move: from credit officer at Banco Mercantil, S.A. (November 1993 to April 1996), credit officer at Intermediaria Financiera, S.A. of Grupo FICOHSA (September to December 1996) and credit officer then agency manager at Banco FICOHSA (January 1997 to February 2003) to President of the Banco Central de Honduras (from 27 January 2018)
records.summary: The central bank's own biography, published by the Central American Monetary Council, lists Cerrato's ten years in Honduran commercial banking before his public career and his appointment as central bank president in January 2018. Ownership: Banco Ficohsa's audited financial statements state the bank is 94.28% owned by Grupo Financiero Ficohsa S.A., domiciled in Panama, which establishes private shareholding; the biography page itself states no ownership.

records.people: Luis Rivas Anduray (Economic Adviser, Banco Central de Nicaragua, 2001-2002)
records.move: from Economic Adviser at the Banco Central de Nicaragua (2001-2002), via the finance ministry's fiscal affairs office (2002-2003), to General Manager of Banpro from late 2004 and now its chief executive and director
records.summary: Revista E&N's profile gives Rivas Anduray's two years as economic adviser at the Banco Central de Nicaragua, his 2002-2003 spell running the finance ministry's fiscal affairs office, and his move to Banpro as general manager at the end of 2004, where he is now chief executive. Ownership: a LexLatin report on the Nueva Tenedora Banpro holding states that Banpro's majority shareholder is Grupo Promerica, of Panamanian origin, describes Promerica as the second Central American financial group of private capital, and says Banpro was owned by the Nicaraguan businessman Ramiro Ortiz Mayorga.
records.source_title: Luis Rivas Anduray, CEO de política de puertas abiertas (Revista Empresas & Negocios)
records.quote: Asesor Económico del Banco Central de Nicaragua durante los años 2001 y 2002
